title: Customer-driven data retirement with cryptographic tombstones and timeline evidence
text:
Customer-driven data retirement with cryptographic tombstones and timeline evidence

description:
Provide customers a self-service, auditable workflow to retire user data on demand that produces verifiable timeline evidence. The core idea is to produce cryptographic tombstones—signed manifests that prove deletion events occurred against a particular tenant/region at a particular time—and a downloadable evidence bundle that legal/compliance teams can consume. The system must respect residency policies, retention overrides, and allow resumable distributed purge jobs across multi-region storage backends.

background:
Existing work has covered scheduled purge orchestration and region-stamped erasure pipelines, but customers still ask for: (1) tenant-initiated deletion with immediate attestable proof, (2) a compact export that auditors can verify independently, and (3) operations that survive interrupted jobs and network partitions. Current PRDs address scheduled purges; this ticket focuses on customer-triggered retirement with cryptographic proof and operational resiliency.

goals:
1) Design an API and Console flow for customer-triggered data retirement that returns a signed deletion manifest. 2) Implement backend orchestration that coordinates per-region workers and emits a tamper-evident evidence bundle. 3) Expose verification CLI and lightweight verifier so customers can independently validate proofs. 4) Ensure retention policy checks and legal hold detection are enforced before any irreversible operation.

non_goals:
1) This work does not change core retention policy storage semantics. 2) It does not attempt to replace legal-hold workflows; if a legal-hold is present the flow will fail with a clear error and next steps. 3) It does not initially provide FIPS-HSM signing; signing will use platform KMS with an audit trail.

success_metrics:
Customers can initiate RTBF-style retirements via API/UI within 2 clicks or 1 API call
Evidence bundle generation latency under 20s for tenant <100GB
Independent verification CLI validates bundle signature and per-region manifests in under 5s
Zero accidental deletions in self-serve trials (tracked via canary cohort)
Customer satisfaction score >= 90% in pilot audits

acceptance_criteria:
API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/retire with optional scope and retention-override returns operation ID and signed tombstone upon completion
Console: UI flow exists in Tenant Settings > Data > Retire with copy explaining legal-hold and residency constraints
Evidence bundle: zipped artifacts include signed manifest(s), per-region deletion receipts, job timeline, and operator runbook reference
Verification: verifier CLI (open-source) validates signatures against published signing key and confirms deletions match requested scope
Resumability: if a purge job is interrupted, restarting using operation ID resumes from last checkpoint without double-delete
Audit logs: tokenized audit events emitted to customer audit sink and internal audit ledger for at least 1 year (configurable)

implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Design): finalize API contract, manifest schema, and KMS signing approach (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Prototype): implement coordinator service that fans out region jobs and collects receipts; produce unsigned bundles for UX testing (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (Signing & Verifier): integrate platform KMS signing and build verifier CLI + CI checks (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (Resumability & Retention Checks): add checkpointing, legal-hold preflight, and safe-guard gates (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (Console + Docs): add UI path, export button, and auditor-facing docs; run pilot with 3 customers (2 weeks)
Phase 6 (Rollout): staged rollout to all tenants with feature flag and monitoring alerts (1 week)

rollout_plan:
Alpha behind feature flag for internal compliance team and SEs
Pilot: 3 customers in NA/EU with support on standby
Gradual ramp: enable 10% of self-serve tenants, monitor metrics and incidents
Full GA after no major regressions and KMS audit sign-off

tradeoffs_and_risks:
Signing with platform KMS provides quick iteration but may not satisfy long-term FIPS/HSM requirements; plan a phased HSM integration
Generating full evidence bundles for very large tenants could be expensive; initially cap bundle generation size and provide streaming exports for large datasets
Resumability adds complexity to worker idempotency; must carefully design tombstone semantics to avoid accidental double-erase
Exposing a verification tool increases transparency but may reveal metadata patterns; manifest design must minimize leaked metadata while remaining auditable
